adrs.title: PostgreSQL as the system of record
adrs.summary: We will use PostgreSQL 15 (managed, Multi-AZ) as the system of record for all player-owned data. Caches and derived stores are allowed but must be rebuildable from PostgreSQL or the event log.

adrs.title: Kafka for domain events
adrs.summary: Chosen option: "Kafka (MSK)", because it gives durable, replayable, partitioned event streams. All cross-service domain events are published to Kafka topics keyed by player id, retained 7 days.

adrs.title: Redis sorted sets as the derived ranking store with PostgreSQL ledger as source of truth
adrs.summary: - O(log n) rank of an arbitrary player (around-me) on boards of 5M–40M entries. - Correctness anchored in the system of record (ADR-0001, NFR-006). - Delivery in 6 weeks with 3 engineers.

adrs.title: Exactly-once scoring via applied-events ledger in the same PostgreSQL transaction
adrs.summary: - Zero double-applied or lost events (FR-002, NFR-006). - Throughput of 20k events/s (NFR-003). - No new infrastructure (6-week constraint).

adrs.title: PostgreSQL-only ranking with keyset seeks and score-bucket counts
adrs.summary: - Correctness by construction for FR-002 and NFR-006 (CRITICAL). - An around-me read in O(log n) (NFR-002). - Delivery in 6 weeks; the fewest moving parts.

adrs.title: PostgreSQL truth with Redis read model using absolute re-asserted writes
adrs.summary: - Ranks that converge to the PostgreSQL truth within a bounded time after any failure (NFR-006). - O(log n) reads without load on the system of record (NFR-002), and freshness ≤ 2 s (NFR-001). - Reuse of the existing des…
